scenes.narration: It is three in the morning, and every screen in the city is still on. This is a demo of the infogen toolkit, and none of the numbers you will see are real.

scenes.title: Made-up spending by sector
scenes.narration: Bar charts grow one bar at a time, and each bar can appear exactly when its name is spoken: first chips, then cloud, then robots.

scenes.title: Pins, routes and countries
scenes.narration: Maps use real country shapes. Highlight France and Germany, drop a pin on Paris, and draw a route to Berlin.
Versus scenes compare two things row by row, and the winner of each row lights up.

scenes.title: A line that draws itself
scenes.narration: Line charts draw from left to right, and an annotation pops up on the point that matters.

scenes.label: A number that counts up
scenes.narration: A single big number counts up, with a line underneath it.

scenes.title: One in four
scenes.label: 5 in 20
scenes.narration: Icon grids make a share easy to see: five people out of twenty.

scenes.title: Timelines scroll
scenes.narration: Timelines add events as they are mentioned: the launch, the boom, the warning, and the crash.

scenes.title: Lists count down
scenes.narration: Lists can count down: number three, number two, and number one.
And illustrations pan, zoom and carry labels, while the time badge stays in the corner.

scenes.text: Every number on screen needs a source.
scenes.narration: One rule above all: every number on screen needs a source.
